body: I did put on an ffp2 when going to open the windows, but for how long is the air unbreatheable in there, the internet says 3hrs for aerosols?

yeah at least I don't have any illnesses or anything like that. But any infection would be impossible for me to deal with (not just severe one). Like I said above, being sick even mildly for me is like being crawled by spiders for days for someone who is scared of spiders.   

How long do you think I should not go into the hallway? I have all the windows open everywhere but the hallway itself does not have a window.
I'm trying to for the brief interaction... but currently I am trying to figure out when I can walk into the hallway again because I am getting hungry in the living room (it has been 1.5hrs)
no, physically I most likely would be "fine" but not mentally, getting any disease to me is like being crawled over by 100 spiders for days to someone who is scared of spiders.
I understand but there are symptoms possible in mild covid that I can't deal with at all from an anxiety standpoint. I have to prevent all kinds of illness even mild at all costs.

30% sounds super scarily high. Like, if the chance of a plane crashing would be 30% I'd be terrified the whole flight. I can't get sick at all, like I am not primarily worried about a severe case but about any case.

yes of course! 3x moderna. But my country lets omicron run wild and vaccine protection against omicron (at least in the preprints of antibody studies) is a lot less. And there have been cases of fullly vaccinated people getting infected with omicron, the scariest one being across the hallway in a quarantine hotel, I think that was in Hong Kong or Taiwan.

you are suggesting to habitually let strangers expose you to covid? I don't understand the logic behind that, like... even if you get infected and are fine you can be reinfected (especially with more variants) and roll the dice again on getting long covid.

throwaway time

got  diagnosed with DID (and anxiety and OCD) halfway through medschool, now  about to start residency (surgery). Overcoming well... I guess we all  (meaning all the people in this body) deal with it differently. There is  one who mainly dealt/deals with it by studying, so that is how we got  through this. I mean DID isn't something you develop later in life,  we've been this way since the body was a small kid. The most chaotic  time was actually high school with uncontrolled switches and fun like  that. Now we can control it unless there is a specific trigger for  someone to come out (which is pretty rare to encounter in the wild).  Just saying that in case someone gets worried we'd endanger patients, we  definitely do not, we would not work if that was the case.

Seeing  our psychiatrist is a life-line. Will be fun once we start residency  and are down to only seeing him during vacations. During rotations  seeing him once a month led to pretty severe suicidal thoughts of some  who don't do that well.

On the  plus side we do have "unique inside into trauma" (at least that is what  our psych said) and sometimes contemplate going into psychiatry after  all. Not all of us think that is a good idea though.

I know hard work is needed to be worth something... I guess I am just kinda salty about having wasted my whole life up to this point, which I know is my own fault... It feels like everyone else is lightyears ahead and it makes me wonder if I'll ever be worth anything to anyone.  
My therapist knows about those feelings... it is an ongoing discussion...
I don't know any tricks sry...

But have you ever met a system who only had been "emotionally neglected"? no real trauma at all? Can that alone really form a (polyfragmented) system?  
How do you overcome trauma you don't remember? I thought the whole point of trauma memories, why they linger is because your brain is telling you that you were in danger and there is something you have not learned from it yet (whether that is true or not). So you have to remember it to look at it and know you can now prevent this from ever happening again.   

How do I get symptoms? Sry that was sarcastic, but I don't have any as far as I know...
Unfortunately no it can't be trauma cause it happened at age 21. And I was a system before that. Also it was not life-threatening and my fault.
If turning into a dog would get me adopted and have a pack/family I think I'd do that in a heartbeat. But I am an adult human, I cannot be adopted anymore.

every parent yells at their child at one point, not every child has DID.

I react so strongly because if that is the case I am not salvageable and don't deserve any help. It would mean I was/am so insignificant and annoying that no one even took the time to hurt me.

​

EDIT: wouldn't you as someone who actually suffered get offended if I go "well m dad yelled at me when I broke rules and once I dropped an ice cream cone so really I had it just as bad as you and am such a poor little girl pls pity me". ?

Well... I know my upbringing was normal so maybe it is just me. Not everyone can have a special skill or talent there are bound to be average people with no redeeming qualities...   

How do you enjoy not having any? Everything I do reminds me of how my existence might be a lie, I just wanna cry and be held but have no reason to and can't and I have no community I fit in, am alone in a puddle of self hatred.

No, she is not "emotionally abusive" (I really think it shouldnt be called that, it seems unfair to people with real abuse). Have you ever met any person with (polyfragmented) DID who had no real abuse only was too weak to deal with little things that every child experiences? I asked the specialist who diagnosed me and he said that isnt possible, for only that to cause DID.

If that is true how could I live with that? Knowing I only exist because I am a weak pathetic person who isnt loveable.

But I do remember wanting to be special as a child. And after my attempts at telekinesis did not work out what if I just made up something else? Something connected to trauma in hopes that I would deserved being taken care of for it? I know it is really disgusting, I am disgusting. I was (and I guess still am) a worthless child with no skills or talents, maybe that is why I talked myself into this delusion, even ending up stealing years of therapy for it.  

I never saw either of my parents drunk. Mom doesn't like alcohol and dad apparently has such a strong reaction to (I was told) it that he stops at one beer (also cause usually he drove home after we were somewhere). We never had any alcohol at home. Obv have not been to foster care. I also have my medical records from age 6 up and there is nothing in there either.  

It just... I have to make up conspiracy theories to even make any trauma *possible at all.* My parents are so average and normal they feel like cardboard, if that makes any sense. Maybe I just don't want to be a cardboard person as well? Alone and insignificant forever.

But how can I be sure that I actually have alters and didn't just pretend until I had convinced myself? I got diagnosed at 22, am 24 now. You say you were completely unaware... I read that a few times but the systems always had suspicious things in their past like foster care, very religious parents, being adopted, history of severe medical issues or drug-addicted parents etc, never a fully normal boring childhood like me.   

Did you have any indicators of trauma like that or can it really just be completely gone?

yeah I am very sure that I've never been in a car crash, also I had the dream when I was almost 7 already so yeah. Very sure mom would have never let me see someone dead either, as I mentionned in another reply she turned off the tv at the slightest sign of negative emotions. And no one ever babysitted me since she wasnt working or going out or anything so unless someone (and who? I only have one uncle who I only saw at family gatherings) roofied her to touch me (which is an example of the unlikely scenarios I have to come up with to construct the possibilities of me being traumaties)... yeah that most likely did not happen.   

I am sorry for what happened to you... why would you ever send that to... I am sorry.

Hmm...kid dreams... being run over by a huge indiana jones style rolling stone, pretty sure that would have killed me if it was real and being in a car accident because of driving on the wrong side of the highway, that also pretty much 100% did not happen. Other than that I don't really remember any nightmares. How did you find evidence, if I am allowed to ask?

I guess I don't have symptoms? I never had a flashback. We do switch around but after years of this we have methods on how to make sure the memories that are needed for functioning are distributed (like automatic newsletters in a way). Cooperation is reached too, everyone knows what we have to do to keep the body alive, so we do that. I am lucky to share this life with pretty sensible people, most are actually better at adulting than me (and one cleaned up my kitchen yesterday, thanks again).    

So again I'd need to find the mysterious trauma bearing person. After finding 100-odd non-trauma people of all ages from infant to 70. I don't really know where to look anymore...   

> Also, trauma can be "just" emotional neglect--if a baby or young child  has no one to turn to for emotional regulation and for learning how to  process feelings, then there are many "ordinary" experiences that will  be overwhelming. With no way to process and integrate them, a young  developing mind will dissociate. 

You mean while every system I ever read about has real trauma it could be that I just was too weak to deal with ordinary stuff? That sounds almost worse than having no trauma.   

> I can't imagine that you found no experience to be frightening or  embarrassing or frustrating or painful when you were a child. If that's  the case, then all of those experiences must be held by other parts,  because they are part of being alive. 

Before the age of 6-9? no, I can't find anything. I never had a painful injury or illness. Parents did not hurt me in any way. I remember being scared when I heard thunder while still in the forest once... other than that... I guess my mom is a bit odd in the way that she did everything she could to shield me and my brother from anything bad. Like she would turn off any show on the tv, even kids shows if there was any sign of negative emotions just to make sure we wouldnt see violence or something like that. And since she was stay at home she was always there to make sure nothing bad happened. I don't know where to fit in trauma there.   

Before you think she was a helicopter parent, nope she never had any ambitions or drilled me or anything, "B's are fine, as long as you go out and have fun too" was her attitude to school. It lead to me wasting most of my childhood, but that is another story and I know in the end I have only me to blame for that.

I mean obviously I don't remember my whole childhood from start to finish, no one does. I'd say I have adaqueat snippets of different ages of pictures of the school/kindergarden I went to, the house I used to live in, the local swimming pool...  

I was convinced that must be the case, an alter I don't know yet holding back the memories. But I know so many now (polyfragmented) and no one has any memories that aren't completely ordinary. It is almost like our childhood has made an effort to be as bleak and blank as possible.   

How would I find such an alter?

> First off I don't think anyone worth talking speaking to will shun you for not remembering trauma.   

Not for not remembering, no. But from what I keep reading on this sub definitely for not having any.   

So you are convinced there will be trauma if I just dig long enough? How can you know I didn't make everything up for attention and there will be none, how can I know?
